about.itaunSubtitle: LA PLATEFORME AFRICAINE DE RÉSEAUTAGE ET D'INNOVATION
about.itaunDesc1: ITAUN (African Networking and Innovation Platform) is an initiative designed to strengthen cooperation between key actors in academia, research, and the private sector across Africa. It brings together international experts and senior African leaders to exchange on innovation, entrepreneurship, competitiveness, and digital transformation.
about.itaunDesc2: ITAUN unites universities, higher education institutions, research structures, and professional training centers to drive inclusive and sustainable innovation across the continent.
about.networkingDesc: Cross-sector cooperation between African universities, public institutions, and private enterprises.
about.expertiseDesc: Exchange platform for experts, higher education institutions, research bodies, and training centers.
about.trainingDesc: Workshops, colloquia, and programs on future-oriented professions in collaboration with strategic partners.
about.fawrDesc: (Forum of African Women Researchers), a flagship initiative aligning with CHIFAA's mission to amplify women's voices in science, technology, and innovation across the continent.
about.siaafDesc: (Semaine de l'IA en Afrique), annual AI week gathering researchers, innovators and policymakers. A natural home for CHIFAA's AI for health ethics conversations.
about.cafDesc: (African Colloquium on Training 4.0), advancing digital education and future-skills development as a driver of African excellence.
about.bamaDesc: (Best African Mobile Application), pan-African student competition fostering tech innovation, with 14 countries and hundreds of participants per edition.
about.whyDesc: ITAUN's pan-African network and CHIFAA's mission converge on shared values: women's empowerment, inclusive technology, and African-centered innovation. Through this partnership, CHIFAA gains access to:
about.benefit1: A network of researchers, academics and health experts across 14+ African countries
about.benefit2: Visibility through SIAAF, FAWR and ITAUN events as showcase platforms
about.benefit3: Institutional credibility with universities, governments, and NGOs
about.benefit4: A pipeline of young African innovators who can contribute to CHIFAA's technology development
about.menaDesc: The MENA Observatory on Responsible AI is an interdisciplinary platform connecting policy-oriented researchers and innovators, aimed at fostering collaboration and building capacity for responsible data and AI practices. Join our diversified regional network to share knowledge, exchange ideas, and advocate for impactful policies that shape the future of AI and data in our region.

founder.subtitle: AI GOVERNANCE EXPERT · FOUNDER OF CHIFAA · AUTHOR
founder.intro: "Technology has a moral responsibility, not only to be intelligent, but to be just. When we design AI with dignity at its centre, we do not simply build better technology. We build a more humane world."
founder.bio1: Maha Jouini sits at a rare intersection, where artificial intelligence meets humanity, and where personal transformation becomes public purpose.
founder.bio2: A digital policy advocate and AI governance expert, Maha currently serves as Digital Communication Officer at the African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD) in Johannesburg, and as Vice President of the Agence Francophone et Africaine de l'Intelligence Artificielle (AFRIA). Her work shapes how AI is designed, governed, and experienced across Africa and the MENA region, always with equity, dignity, and inclusion at the center.
founder.bio3: She holds an MSc in Applied Technology & Artificial Intelligence from Tianjin University of Technology in China, as well as an Executive Master in Data Governance, Cybersecurity and Cloud from HEC Rabat. Her expertise spans AI governance, cloud technologies, digital policy, communication, and human-centered innovation. Her academic and executive training also includes Ethics, Technology, and Public Policy for Practitioners at Stanford University, Advanced AI Policy & Ethics studies at the University of Cape Town, and AI Politics & Digital Justice studies with the CAIDP Centre for AI & Digital Policy in the United States.
founder.bio4: In 2026, she was honoured with the She Shapes AI Award in the AI Thought Leadership category, a recognition that affirmed what has always driven her work: that lived experience is not a footnote to expertise. It is expertise.
founder.bio5: But Maha's story does not begin in a boardroom. It begins with survival, healing, and reinvention. As a cancer survivor currently undergoing hormonal treatment after surgery and radiation, she learned to listen deeply to her body, emotions, and humanity in a world that often rewards exhaustion over wellbeing. That experience transformed not only her life, but also her vision of technology itself.
founder.bio6: That lived reality became the foundation of CHIFAA, a human-centered AI initiative designed for cancer patients and survivors in North Africa. Through CHIFAA, Maha advocates for compassionate, culturally grounded, and inclusive technologies that support women navigating illness with dignity, knowledge, and hope.
founder.bio7: She is also a storyteller, poet, and creative voice from North Africa. As the author of two books, "عاشقة من إفريقية" and "الرقصة الأخيرة من قرطاج إلى المسين", Maha explores identity, memory, belonging, and transformation with the same depth she brings to policy and governance work.
founder.bio8: Beyond technology and policy, she believes creativity itself is a form of healing and resistance. Whether through writing, public speaking, or advocacy, she continues to build bridges between ethics, art, health, and emerging technologies. Maha Jouini does not simply advocate for human-centered AI. She lives it.
